option.name: --all
tip: Do not ignore hidden files (files with names that start with '.')

option.name: --almost-all
tip: In a directory, do not ignore all file names that start with '.', only ignore '.' and '..'

option.name: --author
tip: Show author in long format. On the supported platforms, the author always matches the file owner

option.name: --block-size
tip: scale sizes by BLOCK_SIZE when printing them

option.name: --classify
tip: Append a character to each file name indicating the file type. Also, for regular files that are executable, append '*'. The file type indicators are '/' for directories, '@' for symbolic links, '|' for FIFOs, '=' for sockets, '>' for doors, and nothing for regular files. when may be omitted, or one of: none - Do not classify. This is the default. auto - Only classify if standard output is a terminal. always - Always classify. Specifying --classify and no when is equivalent to --classify=always. This will not follow symbolic links listed on the command line unless the --dereference-command-line (-H), --dereference (-L), or --dereference-command-line-symlink-to-dir options are specified

option.name: --color
tip: Color output based on file type

option.name: --context
tip: print any security context of each file

option.name: --dereference
tip: When showing file information for a symbolic link, show information for the file the link references rather than the link itself

option.name: --dereference-command-line
tip: Do not follow symlinks except when given as command line arguments

option.name: --dereference-command-line-symlink-to-dir
tip: Do not follow symlinks except when they link to directories and are given as command line arguments

option.name: --directory
tip: Only list the names of directories, rather than listing directory contents. This will not follow symbolic links unless one of `--dereference-command-line (-H)`, `--dereference (-L)`, or `--dereference-command-line-symlink-to-dir` is specified

option.name: --dired
tip: generate output designed for Emacs' dired (Directory Editor) mode

option.name: --escape
tip: Use escape quoting style. Equivalent to `--quoting-style=escape`

option.name: --file-type
tip: Same as --classify, but do not append '*'

option.name: --format
tip: Set the display format

option.name: --full-time
tip: like -l --time-style=full-iso

option.name: --group-directories-first
tip: group directories before files; can be augmented with a --sort option, but any use of --sort=none (-U) disables grouping

option.name: --hide
tip: do not list implied entries matching shell PATTERN (overridden by -a or -A)

option.name: --hide-control-chars
tip: Replace control characters with '?' if they are not escaped

option.name: --human-readable
tip: Print human readable file sizes (e.g. 1K 234M 56G)

option.name: --hyperlink
tip: hyperlink file names WHEN

option.name: --ignore
tip: do not list implied entries matching shell PATTERN

option.name: --ignore-backups
tip: Ignore entries which end with ~

option.name: --indicator-style
tip: Append indicator with style WORD to entry names: none (default), slash (-p), file-type (--file-type), classify (-F)

option.name: --inode
tip: print the index number of each file

option.name: --kibibytes
tip: default to 1024-byte blocks for file system usage; used only with -s and per directory totals

option.name: --literal
tip: Use literal quoting style. Equivalent to `--quoting-style=literal`

option.name: --long
tip: Display detailed information

option.name: --no-group
tip: Do not show group in long format

option.name: --numeric-uid-gid
tip: -l with numeric UIDs and GIDs

option.name: --quote-name
tip: Use C quoting style. Equivalent to `--quoting-style=c`

option.name: --quoting-style
tip: Set quoting style

option.name: --recursive
tip: List the contents of all directories recursively

option.name: --reverse
tip: Reverse whatever the sorting method is e.g., list files in reverse alphabetical order, youngest first, smallest first, or whatever

option.name: --show-control-chars
tip: Show control characters 'as is' if they are not escaped

option.name: --si
tip: Print human readable file sizes using powers of 1000 instead of 1024

option.name: --size
tip: print the allocated size of each file, in blocks

option.name: --sort
tip: Sort by `<field>`: name, none (-U), time (-t), size (-S), extension (-X) or width

option.name: --tabsize
tip: Assume tab stops at each COLS instead of 8

option.name: --time
tip: Show time in `<field>`: access time (-u): atime, access, use; change time (-t): ctime, status. modification time: mtime, modification. birth time: birth, creation;

option.name: --time-style
tip: time/date format with -l; see TIME_STYLE below

option.name: --version
tip: Print version

option.name: --width
tip: Assume that the terminal is COLS columns wide

option.name: --zero
tip: List entries separated by ASCII NUL characters
List one file per line

option.name: -c
tip: If the long listing format (e.g., -l, -o) is being used, print the status change time (the 'ctime' in the inode) instead of the modification time. When explicitly sorting by time (--sort=time or -t) or when not using a long listing format, sort according to the status change time

option.name: -C
tip: Display the files in columns

option.name: -f
tip: List all files in directory order, unsorted. Equivalent to -aU. Disables --color unless explicitly specified

option.name: -g
tip: Long format without owner information

option.name: -m
tip: List entries separated by commas

option.name: -o
tip: Long format without group information. Identical to --format=long with --no-group

option.name: -p
tip: Append / indicator to directories

option.name: -S
tip: Sort by file size, largest first

option.name: -t
tip: Sort by modification time (the 'mtime' in the inode), newest first

option.name: -u
tip: If the long listing format (e.g., -l, -o) is being used, print the status access time instead of the modification time. When explicitly sorting by time (--sort=time or -t) or when not using a long listing format, sort according to the access time

option.name: -U
tip: Do not sort; list the files in whatever order they are stored in the directory. This is especially useful when listing very large directories, since not doing any sorting can be noticeably faster

option.name: -v
tip: Natural sort of (version) numbers in the filenames

option.name: -x
tip: List entries in rows instead of in columns

option.name: -X
tip: Sort alphabetically by entry extension

global_option.name: --help
tip: Print help information
